findingClass: a subscription row whose stored timestamp is a zone-less source-local wall-clock string parsed as UTC by a TZ=UTC process — the value lands 5h30m (IST) ahead of the true observation instant. BSE's `Maxdt` varies intraday (e.g. "13:36:42 IST") as well as day-end ("5:00:00 PM"); `new Date(maxdt)` in scrapers/bse-api-scraper.ts before T-999 mis-parsed all of it, but only the day-end 5:00:00 PM case reliably survives to be PERSISTED (W-38's 5-minute-future guard rejects most shifted intraday reads outright), so the recoverable, detectable signature is specifically time-of-day 17:00:00 exactly for scope BSE_ONLY.
failThreshold: any subscriptions row with scope = 'BSE_ONLY' whose "timestamp" time-of-day is exactly 17:00:00.000000 (fixed threshold, not a ratchet: a genuine UTC instant of 17:00:00 is 22:30 IST, a time BSE's exchange session has been closed for hours and never publishes a fresh subscription read at, so no legitimate row can land there) OR whose "timestamp" is more than 5 minutes later than the row's own creation time where that can be measured
unverifiableWhen: never — always runs against the subscriptions table
note: Detection upgrade for T-999 (source-local-time-parsed-in-utc-process class). scripts/repair-bse-subscription-ist-shift.ts repairs the EXISTING rows this check flags (dry-run default, --apply on staging/ipodhan_test only). A future member of the class (a different source, or a different BSE field parsed the same wrong way) is caught by extending the same time-of-day / scope predicate, not by re-typing a new check.
